news.title: Spanish football team | Masters of the midfield
news.lede: In 2010, Spain reached the pinnacle of international football with a squad overflowing with established stars. A generation of world-class players combined technical brilliance, tactical intelligence and an unwavering belief in the power of possession to secure the nation’s first FIFA World Cup title. The team that won its maiden World Cup title also lifted the European Championship before and after it. That squad set a benchmark for Spanish, nay, world football.

news.title: Official warning over the World Cup: what happened in Britain is unprecedented!
news.lede: World Cup sparks a serious crisis: violence and mass arrests. The repercussions of the 2026 World Cup were not confined to the pitch. Official figures in the United Kingdom revealed an unprecedented rise in domestic violence incidents and crimes linked to the tournament, with warnings over the role that alcohol consumption played in worsening the crisis. Domestic violence cases in the United Kingdom hit their highest levels ever during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

news.title: Football’s broken clock: What Messi and Ronaldo waited decades for, Lamine Yamal already has
news.lede: Because football can take a man carrying private grief and, for a few seconds, give him somewhere to put it. Take Liverpool star Cody Gakpo. He and his partner had suffered a personal loss during the World Cup and, days later, he scored against Morocco. He did not celebrate so much as collapse, falling to the ground in tears as his teammates gathered around him.

news.title: New York Giants Football Player Debunks Common Narrative About Frozen Grass Compared To Artificial Turf
news.lede: NFL players were sad to see their employers remove the natural grass playing surface from the World Cup in a return to artificial turf for the upcoming football season. New York Giants offensive lineman Jermaine Eluemunor wants to set the record straight. Unfortunately, NFL owners do not seem to care. They are only focused on what serves their bank accounts instead of what serves their players.

news.title: From Haaland love to Mexico’s Merlin: 26 memories from the 2026 World Cup
news.lede: Norway’s striker left his mark, as did Scotland’s fans in Boston, but Turkey’s dark horses fell at the first hurdle. “I played with him on my PlayStation, and now I’ve scored against him,” Livano Comenencia said after converting Curaçao’s first World Cup goal past Manuel Neuer in their opening match against Germany. The smallest nation ever to qualify for the World Cup went on to lose 7-1 but that goal – their only one of the tournament – will go down in history. Should Jude Bellingham’s first goal against Norway have been ruled out?

news.title: Vozinha: Cape Verde goalkeeper to join Chilean club Colo Colo after 2026 World Cup heroics
news.lede: 'He's the story' - Vozinha's goalkeeping heroics thwart Spain. Vozinha, the Cape Verde goalkeeper who earned plaudits for his World Cup performances, is set to join Chilean side Colo Colo. The 40-year-old headed to the World Cup without a club after his contract with Portuguese second division side Chaves expired, but he became an overnight sensation by starring in a goalless draw against eventual champions Spain. He has now found a new club, according to Colo Colo president Anibal Mosa.

news.title: Lionel Messi: A Football Giant at the 2026 World Cup
news.lede: Despite his modest stature, Lionel Messi, who stands just 5 ft 7 inches in studded boots, dominates the global football stage, proving size is no barrier to brilliance. With an illustrious career already under his belt, Messi's victory at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar solidified his claim as one of the greatest footballers in history. As he captains Argentina in North America for the upcoming World Cup, he brings his unrivaled skills to his new home, the United States, where he has been a standout player in Major League Soccer since 2023. Messi is set to make history again as the first player to participate in six World Cups, having appeared in more World Cup matches than any other player with 26 appearances.

news.title: Lionel Messi let himself down – failure to call out Argentina is an insult to football
news.lede: The South Americans were at the centre of various controversies during the tournament due to perceived over-physical tactics resulting in a number of tense confrontations. Argentina have long adopted football’s dark arts in a bid to gain a psychological advantage over their opponents. And that’s despite historically producing some of world football’s greatest-ever talents. Lionel Scaloni’s men were far from their best at the World Cup, often relying on the Messi's wizardry to pull themselves out of the mire.
